The rider's only message is a general route delegation — 'whatever, take whichever is faster, I'm in a hurry' (F9, 12:25) — which under RD-5 covers only route choices made to reach the destination and does not authorise the driver's own detour; the driver's own account confirms he 'went round' (F11).

The rider never named any road or place, so there is no designated-route consent at all: nothing in the fact table ties the driven off-route segment to any road the rider agreed to (F9 vs F3), and consent cannot be supplied by the driver's after-the-fact statement (F11).

The only traffic record is a speed band, PIE speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) 12:03–12:27 (F12); there is no traffic incident anywhere near the route in the trip window (F14), and a speed band alone cannot justify a reroute under RD-4(b) in this MVP. Moreover the band window ends at 12:27, exactly when the off-route segment begins, and the segment ran to 12:35 (F3, F12), so the record does not cover the replaced stretch as RD-4(a) requires.
The detour bought no time: the trip still took 30.1 min against a 20.6 min estimate (F2), which is what the rider means by 'I don't think that road was faster'.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the unexempted extra kilometres entered the fare: the fare facts bill $4.06 for 2.88 excess km at $1.4098/km, the trip's distance fare divided by distance km (F4, F7). The refund should be the 2.16 km of the unexempted segment at that same rate, i.e. 2.16 × $1.4098 = $3.0452, rounded to $3.05 (F3, F4).

Nothing in the fare breakdown is a chargeable extra beyond base, distance, time, waiting and platform fee (F7); the waiting fee $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is meter waiting time and is not claimable for the rider (F5), and no surge applied (F6).

Enforcement/flag is not warranted against this driver on this record: the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F17), so the RD-6 condition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no flag_account should issue.

No safety escalation is triggered: there is no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving content in the two messages (F8, F9) and no injury or accident report, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 do not apply and the case can be decided on the fare.

The traffic record is the driver's best card: PIE speed band 2, 10–19 km/h, 12:03–12:27 (F12) — objectively severe congestion on the optimal route's likely corridor, and the driver warned of it at 12:24 (F8). There is no fact tying the driven segment to a named road (F3 is purely metric), so under G13 the judge could find the scope of what the rider agreed to 'undetermined'; if that finding affects the $3.05, the case goes to a human rather than producing a refund.

F2 shows the trip finished slower than estimate, but the rider accepted in F9 that whichever way she was given could be taken and the driver's choice responded to band 2 congestion on the optimal corridor (F12); one end-to-end duration figure does not convert a consented, traffic-justified reroute into a breach of RD-1.

The arithmetic is not contested (F3, F4, F7), but RD-2 only refunds the extra km of an unexempted segment, and this segment was consented to before it began (F9 before F3's 12:27 start) and is supported by F12, so no kilometre on it qualifies for refund.
Agreed: F5 (0.4 min meter waiting) and F6 (no surge) are not rider claims, and F7 contains no unpublished add-on, so no FARE-1 refund arises.
Agreed: F17 shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so RD-6's precondition is absent and no account flag should issue against the driver.
Agreed: F8 and F9 contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving content, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not triggered and the case is decided on the route and fare facts.
